correctness.rationale: Exact necessity: six distinct points requires two interior intersections of each of the three straight edges. Projection feet, perpendicular distances and endpoint bounds reduce exactly to the two strict interval cutoffs. Sufficiency: a single radius in the nonempty common interval produces six distinct intersections. Angle-bisector point proves each eligible interval nonempty; vertices cannot contribute six. Rechecked the equilateral and 3-4-5 exact cases, and 5261 independent numerical chord-circle maxima on 270 triangles. No numeric experiment is an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The literature explicitly motivates the full boundary subset J(K,6) and its measure. Determining its exact three interval components for arbitrary triangles is a natural complete geometric classification, beyond an arbitrary test parameter. It reveals the acute/nonacute change in the number of eligible edges and strong shape-dependence: equilateral ratio 7-4sqrt3, right 3-4-5 ratio 65/864, and a degenerating acute family with fraction approaching 1/2. This is not the previously solved best-center count.
